inspection_summary: Inspected all 2070 normalized lines, including every mathematical section, the full references, and terminal OCR debris. The survey develops L-functions from local factors through automorphic representations, isolates GRH, subconvexity, generalized Ramanujan, and Birch-Swinnerton-Dyer as organizing conjectures, then repeatedly shows how families, positivity, trace formulas, representation changes, and function-field geometry turn inaccessible pointwise questions into average, spectral, or equidistribution problems. OCR is lower-confidence and several displayed formulas are damaged, but the accepted spans retain mechanisms stated recoverably in prose; exact formula typography should be checked against the scan before downstream formula-sensitive use.

sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Bibliographic metadata, title, authors, and a damaged contents list; navigation only.

sections_inspected.label: 1 Introduction and Background
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Introduces the local-to-global Euler-product viewpoint through examples, then reframes it adelically using automorphic representations, completed L-functions, tensor products, and functorial constructions.

sections_inspected.label: 2 Fundamental Conjectures
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: States GRH, subconvexity, generalized Ramanujan, and Birch-Swinnerton-Dyer, emphasizing equivalent formulations, known substitutes, local-global consequences, and family-based partial progress.

sections_inspected.label: 3 Function Field Analogues
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Explains geometric and cohomological spectral models for zeros and the role of Frobenius, families, monodromy, tensor powers, positivity, and trace formulas in proved analogues.

sections_inspected.label: 4 Dirichlet L-Functions GL(1)/Q
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Presents average substitutes for GRH and character-sum routes to subconvexity, including mechanisms whose range can exceed what pointwise GRH directly supplies.

sections_inspected.label: 5 Special Values
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Connects central values to positivity, periods, half-integral-weight coefficients, mollified nonvanishing, arithmetic ranks, and spectral deformation.

sections_inspected.label: 6 Subconvexity and Equidistribution
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Uses subconvexity as a bridge to local-global representation by quadratic forms and to equidistribution of arithmetic quantum states.

sections_inspected.label: 7 GL(2) Tools
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Derives the cancellation problem behind convexity, then develops family moments, amplification, off-diagonal analysis, Petersson/Kuznetsov formulas, and density theorems.

sections_inspected.label: 8 Symmetry and Attacks on GRH
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Contrasts universal high-zero statistics with family-dependent low-zero symmetry and assesses spectral interpretations, explicit formulas, families, and positivity as possible GRH routes.

sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Bibliography, author addresses, page markers, and terminal extraction noise; checked for boundaries but not semantic-unit bearing.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Families, symmetry, and positivity as a local-to-global forcing mechanism
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Across number-field bounds and proved function-field RH, embedding a target in a sufficiently rich family exposes symmetries and positive higher constructions whose aggregate constraints can force local parameters or zero magnitudes.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The number-field discussion offers analogies, partial bounds, and speculation; it does not supply the geometric monodromy or analytic control present in the function-field proof.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Subconvexity as an actionable surrogate for inaccessible GRH
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: A power saving over convexity can provide exactly the error control needed for local-global representation and mass equidistribution, even when full zero-location information is unavailable.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Each application depends on a matched conductor aspect, a value/period or coefficient correspondence, and enough uniformity; subconvexity is not asserted to replace every consequence of GRH.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Representation changes expose positivity or estimable structure
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Hard analytic quantities become tractable after being re-expressed as lower-degree factors, squares of coefficients or periods, theta-series components, or trace-formula sums.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Several correspondences are formula-sensitive in this OCR source, and special factorizations such as CM do not extend generically.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Trace formulas as bidirectional arithmetic-spectral interfaces
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Trace-formula ideas can establish spectral existence, translate family averages into exponential sums, transfer cancellation back to spectral density, and compare representations across groups.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The source explicitly reports that available higher-rank analytic trace formulas had not yet achieved the GL(2)-level estimates needed for general subconvexity.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Analytic control of arbitrarily high constructions forces local purity
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Tensor or symmetric powers amplify a deviant local eigenvalue; when all such global constructions have controlled analytic behavior and positive coefficients, a limiting argument can force the local spectrum onto its predicted boundary.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: For number fields the required analytic properties of all symmetric powers are assumed rather than established in the source; the completed proof belongs to the function-field geometric setting.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Central values encode arithmetic and spectral geometry beyond zero location
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Orders of central vanishing, nonvanishing, and central-value size become rank, Fourier coefficient, period, deformation, or eigenstate-distribution information through structure-specific correspondences.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: GRH alone does not decide central vanishing, and some rank consequences in the source remain conditional on BSD or restricted to low vanishing order.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Average theorems can outperform pointwise conjectural input for structured sums
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Orthogonality and averaging can produce cancellation over moduli or spectra in ranges where applying a pointwise GRH-style bound term by term would be insufficient.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The advantage is tied to problems that genuinely average over a compatible family and does not establish the underlying pointwise conjectures.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Spectral interpretation and family analysis are complementary but logically distinct
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The function-field case separates the spectral realization of zeros from the family, symmetry, and positivity analysis that proves purity; the number-field discussion suggests both components may be needed but allows that family constraints could arrive first.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The proposed number-field spaces and proof scenarios are explicitly tentative and must not be promoted to observed evidence or a settled architecture.
